stem: How did factories contribute to economic growth in the United States during the early 1800s?

options.text: Power-driven machinery produced large quantities of goods quickly and inexpensively.
Increases in income closed the wealth gap between the owners of industrial facilities and their employees.
Workers organized labor unions, which allowed them to demand better working conditions.
Government regulations required industrial companies to invest part of their profits and shares in their communities.
Women could become industrial workers, which allowed them to earn an income.
